reading.body:
OptimumHQ is a software company, not a data center operator, and this entry appears to be a source data error rather than AI infrastructure.

The address tagged in OpenStreetMap as a data center belongs to a shared multi-tenant building in Mesa, Arizona. OptimumHQ's own website lists a different address several miles away in Gilbert. The company builds AI-powered ERP and CRM tools for small and midsize businesses, not data center or colocation infrastructure. No public information indicates server capacity, power draw, or compute facilities at either location.

This record cannot be ranked among Arizona's mapped facilities with published power specifications. Of the 56 facilities tagged as data centers in Arizona, only 4 publish power consumption figures, totaling 512 MW. OptimumHQ publishes no such specifications, and research confirms the address returns no business name in reverse geocoding, matching instead a shared building address associated with multiple unrelated entries.

This facility does not factor into analyses of AI infrastructure or power grid constraints. The entry appears to stem from a mistagged OpenStreetMap telecom point rather than a real data center.
